name: Should I replace my bathtub with a tiled shower, or will I regret losing the tub?

mainEntity.name: Should I replace my bathtub with a tiled shower, or will I regret losing the tub?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removing a tub and installing a tiled shower can be worthwhile when the household needs easier entry, more standing space, or a different bathroom layout, but it is not automatically the best choice. The decision depends on available bathrooms, resale priorities, plumbing changes, storage, and the desired entry type. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design offers bathroom remodeling with layout development, fixture coordination, and tile work, so the conversion can be considered as part of the whole room. Key factors: - A tub-to-shower conversion may expose damaged framing or require drain changes. - A low threshold or curbless design can affect floor construction and waterproofing. - Storage, glass, ventilation, and fixture placement need planning. Practical guidance: Decide whether the household still needs a tub elsewhere before removing the only one. Compare a standard shower, low-threshold shower, and tub-shower combination by daily use and project scope. A layout drawing can clarify the tradeoff before demolition begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tub-to-shower conversion can improve entry and standing space, but consider whether another bathroom still has a tub, whether plumbing or floor work will change, and how much storage and splash control you need. Compare standard, low-threshold, and curbless layouts before demolition.
